rationale: This empirical study examines government funding dependence, bureaucratic accountability and client screening in a volunteer Youth Employment Agency in an eastern US city from 1972 to 1976. It has no connection to household or community water or sanitation services or water/sanitation access outcomes, failing Criterion 1 and Criterion 4 (primary exclusion code E01: wrong topic).
plain_vs_narrow_note: Excluded under both narrow and plain readings of Criterion 2 because the study is completely off-topic (youth employment social services rather than household or community water or sanitation service access).

evidence_quotes.quote: assess the relationship between government funding dependence, bureaucratic accountability, & organizational purpose in the volunteer Youth Employment Agency of an eastern US city.

A summary of findings indicates that counselors weed out hard-to-place clients, eg, the youngest, least work-experienced, & least educated, using such mechanisms as lack of encouragement or follow-up.
